# The JPEG entropy coder's corpus: levels in, bytes out.
#
# **This half of the encoder is exact.** Given the same levels and
# the same code tables, T.81 F.1.2 determines the bitstream
# completely, so unlike the transform there is a right answer and
# this file holds it. The bytes were produced by a Python model of
# F.1.2 that was itself checked by building whole greyscale JPEGs
# with it and having ffmpeg decode them -- 40.5 dB against the
# original at a flat quantisation table of 16, with ffmpeg
# reporting nothing.
#
# The tables are Annex K's, taken from the `DHT` segments of a file
# ffmpeg wrote with `-huffman default` rather than typed out here:
# 162 AC symbols is a great deal to copy by hand and a copy is not
# a second opinion. They are stored as `DHT` stores them, as a
# count of codes per length and then the symbols, and the test
# derives the codes by T.81 C.2 -- so the derivation is checked too.
#
# One record per case. Each is a whole scan: the blocks in order,
# then a flush, so the byte stream is self-contained and the DC
# predictor's behaviour across blocks is covered.
#   case   <name>
#   levels <64 signed decimals>      -- repeated, one line per block
#   bytes  <hex>
